candidates.summary: the gate 404s /u/docs, and /docs — a shipped alias serving 200 on gno.land today — points there
candidates.failure_scenario: GET https://gno.land/docs answers 200 right now and renders the /u/docs page (body title "gno.land - /u/docs"); it is gnoweb's own DefaultAliases entry (app.go:30, "/docs" -> "/u/docs"). On gnoland-1 the namespace holds no packages and ResolveName("docs") is (false bool), so with this branch the same URL returns 404 "user not found" for every visitor and crawler until #5760 serves the embedded docs there. The ADR names the consequence; the decision to ship the 404 before the replacement exists is the reviewer's.

candidates.summary: the shape gate compiles gnolang.Re_name, not the registry's own rule, and runs before both other rules
candidates.failure_scenario: The ADR says taking the shared expression "means gnoweb cannot start refusing names the chain has begun to accept". The chain's rule is not gnolang.Re_name: r/sys/users validates with its own regexp literal, examples/gno.land/r/sys/users/store.gno:27 `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*([_-][a-z0-9]+)*$`, in a realm that is upgraded without redeploying gnoweb (a .gno realm cannot import gnovm/pkg/gnolang, so the two can only ever be copies that agree today). The day the registry widens its rule, gnoweb answers 404 before it asks the chain anything: the shape check at 608 precedes both the ListPaths rule and ResolveName, so a user who is registered, and even one whose namespace holds packages, loses their page until gnoweb is redeployed.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'reName = regexp.MustCompile' examples/gno.land/r/sys/users/store.gno and confirm no gnolang import is possible from a realm; then call GetUserView with a name the registry rule accepts but Re_name rejects and observe the 404 at handler_http.go:609 with no RPC issued
candidates.evidence: store.gno:27 carries its own literal, and store.gno:19-25 documents it as mirroring gnolang's Re_name by hand; the gate at handler_http.go:606-609 runs before buildContributions and userExists.
